title: The canonical contact report
statement: The Book Which Tells the Truth explicitly reports that its speakers are biological beings like terrestrial humans living on another planet, glosses Elohim as those who came from the sky, and reports that the civilization's scientists selected Earth and artificially created terrestrial life, including humanity; this record asserts what the source reports, not that the reported events occurred.

includes: The report layer of TBWTT-1:53 and TBWTT-2:5: what the inspected project digitization explicitly states
The source's gloss of Elohim and its creation narrative as source content

The claim-model consequence: this record is the source_report basis on which woh-claim-0001's hypothesis discipline stands, extracted from that claim so its source criticism can be reviewed independently
excludes: The historicity of the reported encounter or creation programme, which belongs to woh-claim-0001 and its evidence discipline
The publication and founding history of the contact reports, recorded by woh-claim-0020
The identification of the reported beings with the referents of biblical Elohim, retained by woh-claim-0001
The Hebrew semantics of Elohim: the gloss is source content, not a philological derivation
Every other statement in the canon, carried by the claims that cite it

source_references.locator: The standard academic study of the movement; the genre placement of the contact reports within 1970s contactee literature and the composition-account explanations
Régis Dericquebourg, "Rael and the Raelians" — the scholarly account of the movement and its foundational reports

alternatives.statement: The cited passages, read in their edition context, do not support this summary of the reported content; the record mischaracterizes or selectively quotes the source.
Printed French and English editions materially differ from the inspected project digitization, so the reported wording is an artifact of one representation rather than a stable report.

revision_triggers: Edition collation or a corrected project digitization materially changes the wording or location of TBWTT-1:53 or TBWTT-2:5. Collation against the 2005 French and English combined editions was performed by woh-claim-0070-review-0001 and changed nothing material; the 1973 and 1974 first printings remain uncollated and are the live case for this trigger.
Public prose cites this record as if it established the historicity of the reported encounter or creation — the record's one forbidden use; that assertion belongs to woh-claim-0001.
A source-critical review of the Raëlian corpus — the load-bearing question identified by the woh-claim-0001 evidence map — advances, changing what this report layer can carry.
